t: The Republic was proclaimed on 14 April 1931, two days after republicans won a landslide in the municipal elections, and King Alfonso XIII went into exile.
The Constitution of 1931 ended Catholicism's status as the state religion, allowed divorce, extended the vote to women and gave every region the right to autonomy.
A military uprising on 17 July 1936 began the Spanish Civil War, in which an estimated half a million people died, and the Republic was dissolved on 1 April 1939.
dyk: In the Revolution of 1934 the miners of Asturias, in the towns they held, officially declared a proletarian revolution and abolished regular money; the rising lasted two weeks before the army crushed it.
ev: Two days after the municipal elections, the Second Republic is proclaimed and King Alfonso XIII goes into exile
The new Constitution, drafted by a Constituent Cortes, comes into force in December
Catalonia is granted autonomy, with a parliament and a president of its own
The Spanish Confederation of the Autonomous Right (CEDA) wins the elections, opening the "black biennium"
The entry of three CEDA ministers into the government sets off the Revolution of 1934, crushed in Asturias by the army
The Popular Front wins the general election of 16 February
An army uprising in Spanish Morocco on 17 July begins the Spanish Civil War
Madrid falls in March, and the Republic is dissolved after surrendering to the Nationalists

f.founder: The republican parties of the Pact of San Sebastián; Niceto Alcalá-Zamora headed the provisional government
f.predecessor: The monarchy of King Alfonso XIII (the dictatorship of Miguel Primo de Rivera had fallen in 1930)
f.successor: The Nationalist regime of Francisco Franco; a Republican government in exile survived until after the restoration of democracy in Spain
